subject: HIN
label: Grade 03
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 03 Hindi, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Reading short passages
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Reading short passages', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read and answer questions. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Reading short passages' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and answer questions, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: गद्यांश पढ़ें; मुख्य भाव एक वाक्य में लिखें; प्रश्नों के उत्तर गद्यांश के शब्दों में दें; एक उचित शीर्षक सुझाएँ। Method: Model run for 'Reading short passages'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read and answer questions: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Read this short passage I wrote. सुबह का समय था। गीता अपनी दादी के साथ बगीचे में गई। वहाँ गुलाब के फूल खिले थे। गीता ने दादी के लिए एक फूल तोड़ा। [It was morning. Geeta went to the garden with her grandmother. Rose flowers were blooming there. Geeta picked a flower for her grandmother.]

Step 2, Understand the sentences. सुबह का समय था [It was morning] tells when. बगीचे में [in the garden] tells where. गुलाब के फूल [rose flowers] tells what. दादी के लिए [for grandmother] tells for whom. Find these words in the text.

Step 3, Answer questions in full sentences. गीता किसके साथ गई? [Who did Geeta go with?] गीता अपनी दादी के साथ गई। [Geeta went with her grandmother.] फूल कहाँ खिले थे? [Where were the flowers blooming?] फूल बगीचे में खिले थे। [The flowers were blooming in the garden.]

Step 4, Find the reason or result. गीता ने फूल किसके लिए तोड़ा? [For whom did Geeta pick the flower?] उसने दादी के लिए फूल तोड़ा। [She picked the flower for her grandmother.] Always take the answer from the passage, using its own words.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child answers फूल कहाँ खिले थे? with तालाब में [in the pond]. Correction: reread; the text says बगीचे में, so the answer is फूल बगीचे में खिले थे। Another error is leaving out the final vertical line; end every answer with।

Step 6, Your turn: answer what time it was and what Geeta did. Model answer: सुबह का समय था। गीता ने दादी के लिए एक फूल तोड़ा। [It was morning. Geeta picked a flower for her grandmother.] Both answers come directly from the passage.

modules.title: Nouns and gender
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Nouns and gender', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: tell nouns and their gender. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Nouns and gender' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: tell nouns and their gender, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: In 'Mira has a dog called Bruno', 'dog' is a common noun, 'Mira' and 'Bruno' are proper nouns and need capital letters. Method: Model run for 'Nouns and gender'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Tell nouns and their gender: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, A noun (संज्ञा) names a person, animal, thing or place. Each Hindi noun is masculine (पुल्लिंग) or feminine (स्त्रीलिंग). लड़का [boy] and घोड़ा [horse] are masculine. लड़की [girl] and चिड़िया [bird] are feminine.

Step 2, Use the ending as a clue. Many masculine nouns end in ा: लड़का, कमरा [room], बस्ता [bag]. Many feminine nouns end in ी: रोटी, कुर्सी, घड़ी [watch]. Make pairs: बेटा and बेटी, घोड़ा and घोड़ी. Say them aloud.

Step 3, Learn the exceptions. पानी [water], हाथी [elephant] and दही [curd] end in ी but are masculine: हाथी बड़ा है। [The elephant is big.] मेज़ [table] and किताब [book] are feminine: किताब अच्छी है। [The book is good.]

Step 4, Show gender through the verb. लड़का खेलता है। [The boy plays.] लड़की खेलती है। [The girl plays.] The verb ending changes from ता to ती. Sort these: फूल, मेज़, पेड़, कुर्सी. Masculine: फूल, पेड़. Feminine: मेज़, कुर्सी.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says यह मेज़ अच्छा है। Correction: यह मेज़ अच्छी है। because मेज़ is feminine. Another says पानी ठंडी है। Correction: पानी ठंडा है। because पानी is masculine.

Step 6, Your turn: name the gender of घड़ी, बस्ता, चिड़िया and घोड़ा. Model answer: घड़ी is feminine, बस्ता is masculine, चिड़िया is feminine, घोड़ा is masculine. Then write: घड़ी छोटी है। [The watch is small.] with the matching ending.

modules.title: Poems and stories
modules.outcome: recite a poem and retell a story
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Poems and stories', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: recite a poem and retell a story. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Poems and stories' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: recite a poem and retell a story, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: कविता की पंक्तियों में तुक खोजें (जैसे आम और शाम), कवि का भाव बताएँ और भावार्थ अपने शब्दों में लिखें। Method: Model run for 'Poems and stories'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Recite a poem and retell a story: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Read a four-line poem I made. काले बादल, गरजे ज़ोर, नाचे जंगल में हर मोर। छम-छम बूँदें, मीठी तान, खुश हुआ सारा जहान। [Black clouds thunder loudly, every peacock dances in the forest. Pitter-patter drops, a sweet tune, the whole world is happy.]

Step 2, Understand the rhyme. ज़ोर and मोर rhyme, and तान and जहान end with the same sound ान. Mark the rhyming ends with a pencil. Say the lines with a steady beat, and slow down at the rhyming words.

Step 3, Recite with expression. Say गरजे ज़ोर loudly and छम-छम बूँदें softly. Use your hands to show the clouds. Speak clearly, say each word in full, and pause at each comma. Recite twice, then try without the book.

Step 4, Now retell a tiny story. एक नन्हा बीज था। उसे मिट्टी में बो दिया गया। बारिश हुई और वह पौधा बन गया। [There was a tiny seed. It was sown in the soil. It rained and it became a plant.] Use pehle, phir, ant mein: पहले, फिर, अंत में.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child retells the story as बारिश हुई, बीज बन गया पौधा, मिट्टी में बोया. Correction: tell it in order: पहले बीज को मिट्टी में बोया गया, फिर बारिश हुई, अंत में वह पौधा बन गया।

Step 6, Your turn: say the story again using पहले, फिर and अंत में. Model answer: पहले एक नन्हा बीज मिट्टी में बोया गया। फिर बारिश हुई। अंत में बीज पौधा बन गया। [First a tiny seed was sown. Then it rained. Finally the seed became a plant.]

modules.title: Writing sentences
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Writing sentences', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: write sentences about a picture. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Writing sentences' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: write sentences about a picture, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: मेरा नाम अमन है। मैं स्कूल जाता हूँ। यह मेरी किताब है। शब्द: कलम, किताब, गेंद। Method: Model run for 'Writing sentences'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Write sentences about a picture: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Look at a picture of a park with children, a swing, a dog and a girl with a ball. Name what you see: बच्चे [children], झूला [swing], कुत्ता [dog], गेंद [ball], लड़की [girl]. Make a word list before writing sentences.

Step 2, Write what is there. चित्र में एक पार्क है। [In the picture there is a park.] वहाँ एक झूला है। [There is a swing there.] पास में एक कुत्ता बैठा है। [Nearby a dog is sitting.] Use है for one thing and हैं for many.

Step 3, Write what is happening with रहा, रही, रहे. बच्चे झूला झूल रहे हैं। [The children are swinging.] लड़की गेंद से खेल रही है। [The girl is playing with a ball.] कुत्ता भाग रहा है। [The dog is running.]

Step 4, Add colour and feeling. लड़की की गेंद लाल है। [The girl's ball is red.] सब बहुत खुश हैं। [Everyone is very happy.] Put the sentences in order: place first, then what people do, then how they feel.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes लड़की खेल रहा है। Correction: लड़की खेल रही है। because लड़की is feminine. Another writes बच्चे झूल रहा हैं। Correction: बच्चे झूल रहे हैं। because बच्चे is plural.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences about a picture of a market with a woman buying mangoes. Model answer: चित्र में एक बाज़ार है। एक औरत आम खरीद रही है। दुकानदार आम तौल रहा है। [In the picture there is a market. A woman is buying mangoes. The shopkeeper is weighing mangoes.]

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Reading short passages), and at which Bloom level is it?
'read', at the Remember level. (Covered in unit 1: Reading short passages.)
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36. (Covered in: Assessment plan, near the top of this page.)
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Writing sentences) run?
Weeks 28 to 36. (Covered in unit 4: Writing sentences.)
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard. (Covered in: How you are checked, further down this page.)
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
